The claim states that for non-obtuse triangles, the relative circum-center is computed using the analytic formula [S1]. The evidence in Source [S1] explicitly provides the analytic formula for the circum-center relative to vertex a (m_tri) in Equation (3). It further states that for 'remaining obtuse triangles' (implying those that are not obtuse, i.e., non-obtuse, after handling degenerate cases), one should approximate the circum-center. Therefore, the analytic formula is indeed the method used for non-obtuse triangles, as the approximation is reserved for the obtuse cases. All facts in the claim are present and supported by the evidence.

Numerically stable for non-degenerate triangles when using coordinate differences [S1, unofficial].

The claim states that the method is numerically stable for non-degenerate triangles when using coordinate differences. Source [S1] explicitly states that the formula for the circum-center of a triangle (Eq. 3) is 'expressed in differences of coordinates rather than the absolute values' and notes that this reduces relative error because vertices are nearer to each other than to the origin. It further clarifies that the method is unstable only if the denominator vanishes, which occurs when triangles are 'near degenerate'. Therefore, for non-degenerate triangles, the use of coordinate differences supports numerical stability as described.
